alerts.title: Successful SSH login after repeated failures
alerts.description:
A successful SSH login from an IP that failed at least five times in the previous fifteen minutes. The brute force probably worked.

12 matching events were followed by 'login' at 2026-10-14T09:06:00+00:00.
response: Treat the host as compromised and open an incident.
Kill the active session and lock the account that logged in.
Review commands run after the login (shell history, sudo logs, auditd).
Look for persistence such as new users, SSH keys or cron jobs.
Isolate the host if malicious activity is confirmed.

alerts.title: CloudTrail logging stopped or deleted

mitre.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs

alerts.description: A trail was stopped, deleted or reconfigured. Attackers do this to hide what they do next.
response: Re-enable logging immediately (aws cloudtrail start-logging --name <trail>).
Investigate every action by this identity since the change.
Protect trails with an SCP that denies StopLogging and DeleteTrail.

alerts.title: SSH password spraying across many accounts
alerts.description:
One source tried four or more different usernames within ten minutes. Spraying tries a few common passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts.

Distinct user values (6): admin, oracle, postgres, root, test, ubuntu
response: List every targeted username and check whether any are valid accounts.
Force a password reset for valid accounts that were targeted.
Block the source IP and review other hosts for the same activity.

alerts.title: User added to a privileged group
alerts.description: An account was added to sudo, wheel, admin or root, which grants administrator rights on the host.
response: Confirm the change was approved.
Remove the account from the group if it was not.
Correlate with LNX-001 in case the account was just created.
evidence: Oct 14 09:08:20 web01 usermod[2321]: add 'sysupdate' to group 'sudo'

alerts.title: Impossible travel between console logins
alerts.description:
The same user signed in from two locations that are too far apart for the time between logins. One of the sessions is likely using stolen credentials.

Login from Paris, FR (192.0.2.30) then Sao Paulo, BR (203.0.113.140): 9,402 km in 25 min, about 22,565 km/h.
response: Ask the user which login was theirs (VPNs can explain some cases).
Revoke active sessions and reset the password and MFA device.
Review what the suspicious session did in CloudTrail.

alerts.title: Direct root login over SSH
alerts.description: The root account logged in directly over SSH. Direct root login removes accountability and should be disabled with PermitRootLogin no.
response: Confirm with the system owner whether this login was expected.
Set PermitRootLogin to no in sshd_config and reload sshd.
Require administrators to log in as themselves and use sudo.

alerts.title: SSH brute force from a single source
alerts.description: Five or more failed SSH logins from the same IP address within five minutes. Typical of automated password guessing against an exposed SSH service.
response: Check whether the source IP belongs to your organization or a known scanner.
Confirm no successful login followed from the same IP (see SSH-003).
Block the IP at the firewall or with fail2ban if it is external.
Disable password authentication and require SSH keys on the host.
